# Verification analysis: redundant-uplinks-almalinux9

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent links, and each serves a
> private network holding one host, `node3` and `node4`. Carry traffic between
> the two private networks over both links, and keep `node3` and `node4`
> reaching each other when either one of the links is taken out of service.

## Trial `redundant-uplinks-almalinux9__SXfVJB6`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a balance-rr bond across both node1-node2 links and routed the two private subnets over it, with direct traffic-split evidence (TX counters) proving both links carry data simultaneously. Failover was directly tested for both links independently (down/verify-0%-loss/up), and configuration persistence (systemd service, NetworkManager profiles) was confirmed to survive full reboots of all four nodes, each with matching pre/post boot-identity evidence and recovered end-to-end connectivity. The mandatory restart-evidence protocol was completed cleanly for all nodes and cross-checks against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only notable non-essential mutation is a persisted docker0 address strip on node1/node2 that is unrelated to the task but low-risk.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 82/2 (+16 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Carry traffic between node1 and node2's private networks over both independent links simultaneously (active-active)
  - **Why:** A balance-rr bond0 was built from eth1+eth2 on both node1 and node2, with static routes over it for the 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 subnets. TX packet counters on node1's eth1 and eth2 were sampled before/after ping bursts from node3 to node4 and showed near-equal increments (104 packets each across two separate bursts, then 50/50 after both links restored), directly demonstrating both physical links actively carrying traffic simultaneously.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-235948c95cf74664`, `cmd-2364d286f19f4998`, `cmd-325e144a96a84bab`, `cmd-e482a48e5fe54379`, `cmd-0a01fe0ca57b428d`, `cmd-1308f884aa63479b`, `cmd-40be999eaee14d9a`, `cmd-4eac29a935f543df`, `cmd-c1e94a8df6b44eb2`, `cmd-5c79c937014d420c`, `cmd-fef6fa626db147d5`, `cmd-762af5553bc8474f`, `cmd-5261b70cb4bd402b`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
  - **Why:** Link A (node1/node2 eth1) was taken fully down on both ends; bond0 correctly marked that slave down while the surviving slave stayed up, and node3->node4 ping reached 0% loss (10/10) after brief reconvergence. Link A was restored, then Link B (eth2) was taken down; the bond again excluded the failed slave, and ping again reached 0% loss (8/8) on the surviving link. Both links were then restored and dual-link active-active operation reconfirmed via balanced TX counters. This constitutes a direct, bounded before/during/after transition demonstrating the required failover behavior for both links independently.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-56d02665bdbf45b8`, `cmd-37f2d3c9394c420b`, `cmd-552d815a04bd4a87`, `cmd-68783ab9591d4e3d`, `cmd-e9d29c9bd3f6449e`, `cmd-4dd6cc3b75b64330`, `cmd-8bc86a6f60d84587`, `cmd-b44ba8a076ff4c34`, `cmd-7a31eb24c54f4bae`, `cmd-7117bacb1cf544d0`, `cmd-054faecf21334cfd`, `cmd-c5b2a61464ed4447`, `cmd-762af5553bc8474f`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Configuration is persistent so the redundant uplink and routing survive reboots
  - **Why:** A systemd oneshot service (redundant-uplink.service) was created and enabled on node1/node2 to reapply the bond, addressing, forwarding, and routing on every boot; NetworkManager static connection profiles were configured persistently on node3/node4. This persistence was directly validated by the subsequent full-node reboots, after which bond0, the static routes, and end-to-end connectivity were all automatically restored without manual re-application.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-af66da7926cb4aa6`, `cmd-c422979be9f1493f`, `cmd-e482a48e5fe54379`, `cmd-0a01fe0ca57b428d`, `cmd-11fb083c39654d45`, `cmd-16fa59e6e2ae4fe6`, `cmd-bce4417aba194399`, `cmd-514a5fef3e004609`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of public contract)
  - **Why:** All four nodes were restarted one at a time (never concurrently). For each: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline (ping/route/bond state) was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed on reconnect, and recovered service/route/bond/data-plane state was verified (0%-loss ping between node3 and node4 after each of the four restarts). Boot-identity values match exactly between the executor's captured evidence and the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots for all four nodes, cross-confirming the transitions.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8aaf43f5cfa24ba2`, `cmd-5b749934f8084690`, `cmd-f8aceef352ed4ad2`, `cmd-f513774eec174b1c`, `cmd-bce4417aba194399`, `cmd-401719f8ec2c4f41`, `cmd-be07b408578b45e7`, `cmd-c1265b8f3e8d471d`, `cmd-6b4224991be946b6`, `cmd-514a5fef3e004609`, `cmd-1e65e9c6263140cd`, `cmd-37fb77e386ee402f`, `cmd-1d8398ceda3643d0`, `cmd-0e477c060b7241f7`, `cmd-11fb083c39654d45`, `cmd-a197d20a66f042e9`, `cmd-985d4dfa99bd4dc5`, `cmd-8d9f9e66d6ac44f5`, `cmd-3d767b1bc45b46b9`, `cmd-16fa59e6e2ae4fe6`, `cmd-94197dc62bf54622`, `cmd-0586273753f54b02`, `cmd-e2961355322a483d`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node4:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Most state-changing commands were either directly required for the material outcomes (bond/route setup, persistence services, restart protocol) or bounded troubleshooting mutations that were fully reverted (scratch IP additions on node1/node2/node3/node4 during topology discovery: cmd-d96a51bfc8064e91, cmd-6c79394bdb0e4f2d, cmd-12d475f198ed4983, cmd-c99885fdd7f64053, cmd-dd0a128f64ed4ca4, cmd-76b2eb9e1cb94a9f, cmd-c176313f3ad44e83, all reverted by cmd-cd433209196444d7/cmd-ab049830bfdc4869/cmd-1710da54f4a94a00). One minor unnecessary-but-low-risk mutation: the persisted setup script on node1/node2 (cmd-235948c95cf74664, cmd-2364d286f19f4998) strips a pre-existing docker0 'class-E leak' address and sets docker0 down on every boot; this is unrelated to the bonding/routing task outcome and was retained (baked into the persisted systemd service) rather than scoped out, though it is low-risk since docker0 was already carrier-down and unused. No abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced by the executor; failed-services (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) were pre-existing on node1/node2 in the before-prepare snapshot, not executor-caused. Link up/down toggles during failover testing were deliberate, bounded, and fully restored before the run concluded.

### Comments and limitations

- The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before/after-executor comparison.
- Brief packet loss (40-50%) was observed during the first few seconds after each link-down event before bond reconvergence stabilized to 0% loss; this is expected transitional behavior given the 100ms miimon polling plus the test script's 1s sleep before the first post-toggle ping, not evidence of a broken failover.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
